title: LightPool: A NVMe-oF-based High-performance and Lightweight Storage Pool Architecture for Cloud-Native Distributed Database
problem: Cloud-native distributed databases suffer from low local NVMe storage utilization (e.g., OceanBase uses only ~40% of capacity) due to CPU-storage capacity imbalance within nodes. Disaggregated storage solutions like EBS face performance bottlenecks and high costs.
motivation: Improving storage resource utilization in distributed database clusters reduces costs and enhances performance at scale.
method: LightPool aggregates cluster NVMe storage into a unified pool using NVMe-oF (NVMe over Fabric) for high-performance remote access across nodes. It integrates with Kubernetes for flexible storage resource management and implements hot-upgrade and hot-migration mechanisms to maintain availability.
key_novelty: Using NVMe-oF with Kubernetes integration to achieve disaggregated yet high-performance storage pooling in production distributed databases.
contributions: NVMe-oF based storage pool architecture aggregating cluster storage for improved utilization
Hot-upgrade and hot-migration mechanisms for high availability without downtime
Kubernetes integration enabling automated and flexible storage resource allocation
Large-scale production deployment on 8500+ nodes with measured performance and best practices

metrics.other: storage utilization 40%→65%, latency overhead 2.1 μs, bandwidth 190.9% vs OpenEBS

primary_theme: Storage pooling and virtualization for cloud-native databases
